scope: Original 2020 Dune: Imperium base 2–4 multiplayer, including mandatory two-player House Hagal; no solo, variants, expansions, promos or Uprising.
independence: Did not read any summary, reader response, grade or prior reviewer report. Read the prescribed question/key files and ledger. Read the full prescribed extraction, used PDF text to verify pages 7,16–19 and visually checked page7; solo-only page20 was excluded from conclusions. Web checks were used only to investigate Guild Envoy scope, and are distinguished from the authoritative local rules.
verdict: NOT SATURATED: one distinct public-information procedure is untested, and Q52 contains one out-of-scope Uprising clause. All other tested rule claims were supported within the requested scope; no other qualifying additions were found.

findings.title: Supply visibility is an untested information rule
findings.detail: Main p5 setup G6 requires remaining player components in the player supply to be in clear view of all players. Q02 asks starting quantities and positions; Q22 asks unlimited resources/finite troops; Q64 asks decks, Row, Reserve, Mentat, Alliances and first player. None requires the visibility restriction. Q34 explicitly tests the different hidden-information treatment for Intrigues, without addressing component supply visibility. A learner could answer all64 correctly while believing spare components or resource supply may be hidden.

findings.title: Guild Envoy belongs to Uprising
findings.detail: Q52 and its key include Guild Envoy mandatory discard. That is an actual FAQ ruling, but the named card is from Uprising, not original2020 base. The combined FAQ is not itself a base-only card list. Retain the Double Cross and Gun Thopter portions and remove Guild Envoy from this base-only question/key. Do not replace it with Guild Administrator, whose text is different.
findings.proposed_fixed_question: What restrictions apply to Double Cross and Gun Thopter even if other parts of the card could operate?
findings.proposed_fixed_answer: Double Cross requires at least one opponent troop in the Conflict, but you need not have a troop in your own supply. An opponent with no garrisoned troops is unaffected by Gun Thopter’s Agent box.

proposed_questions.question: How must unused player components in a player’s supply be presented to the other players? Does that make the faces of that player’s Intrigue cards public?
proposed_questions.fixed_answer: Keep remaining player components in the player’s supply in clear view of all players. Intrigue cards are a separate exception: keep them face down and separate from the deck; their owner may inspect them, and reveals them to opponents when played.
proposed_questions.novelty: A distinct public-information restriction on player supplies. This is not component-count trivia, altered arithmetic or a recombination of an already-tested outcome. Q34 covers hidden Intrigues; Q02/Q22/Q64 do not cover visible player components.
proposed_questions.recommendation: Accept public-supply visibility as the new fact; the Intrigue clause is a contrast to prevent overgeneralizing visibility and does not itself count as new coverage.

ledger_assessment: The broad source maps and later Q60–Q64 appendices cover most earlier omissions. However, the claim of complete setup mapping misses p5G6 visibility, and the purported base-only p2 FAQ selection incorrectly includes Guild Envoy. Preserve history when versioning both corrections; historical zero-addition passes are observations, not proof of saturation.
limitations: The local rules and combined FAQ do not supply an explicit set index for every named card. Guild Envoy set membership was corroborated externally, with publisher-rule versus external-set evidence distinguished above. No unsupported alteration to base-game rules was proposed.
